caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: CRCNS:pfc-2
attempts.paper_title: Behavior-dependent short-term assembly dynamics in the medial prefrontal cortex
attempts.entry_title: Behavior-dependent short-term assembly dynamics in the medial prefrontal cortex (Fujisawa et al. 2008)
attempts.summary: In this data the paper's trajectory-specific firing held in part: many prefrontal neurons fire differently on left and right trials, but in larger fractions than reported. Its monosynaptic connection results did not reproduce, as the jitter test here found far more excitatory connections and far fewer interneurons, with a bin width and test band the paper does not give. Position-dependent transmission was above chance but in 6.4% of connections against 19.5%, and the split into depressing and facilitating connections and the supralinear effect of coincident inputs did not reproduce. Task performance could not be tested, as only correct trials are deposited. Smaller results on field size, retrospective coding, running speed and spatial clustering reproduced.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Fujisawa, Amarasingham, Harrison and Buzsaki (2008) on both of the paper's datasets, DANDI:000067 (NWB files of the sorted units, the wideband signal and the head LEDs of three rats) and CRCNS pfc-2 (the lab's per-session summaries with the correct trials, the linearised position, the cell lists and, for the paper's Figure 2a session, its list of connections). It covers unit counts, position-dependent and trajectory-selective firing, population measures, odor and speed effects, the jitter test for monosynaptic connections, cell classes, position-dependent spike transmission, facilitation and depression, and presynaptic coincidence.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Fujisawa et al. (2008) from DANDI:000067 and CRCNS pfc-2
Findings of fujisawa-2008-02 checked on CRCNS pfc-2

outcomes.statement: The recording channels of DANDI:000067 can be assigned to the prefrontal probe, the CA1 probe and the nose-poke sensors by the channel map of the CRCNS pfc-2 description of the same recordings (channels 1 to 64 prefrontal, 65 to 96 CA1, 97 right and 98 left nose-poke sensors), and the data agree with that map.
outcomes.source: Methods, Surgery and recording (8-shank, 64-site probe in mPFC); CRCNS pfc-2 data description, version 0.7
outcomes.notes: Check (i) holds in all 12 sessions with a wideband signal in DANDI:000067 (median theta ratio of channels 65 to 96 between 0.41 and 0.67, of channels 1 to 64 between 0.13 and 0.34). Check (ii) holds in the six EE and three FF sessions with a signal (the trial's side sensor is the more active in every trial) and fails in GG.069, GG.097 and GG.149 (0.30, 0.42 and 0.42), where channels 97 and 98 are equally active on left and right trials. A search over every channel from 97 on finds no sensor in GG (best agreement 0.68 to 0.78), so no per-rat correction exists; the NWB files of GG label channels 97 to 101 as neural. EE.088 has no wideband signal in DANDI:000067 and was not checked.
deviations: Check (i) uses one 52 s chunk of the signal per session (the one holding the most trial time) and trial segments of at least 2 s within it; check (ii) uses the mean absolute deviation of the sensor channels from their median, in 1 ms blocks, from the first poke start to the last poke end.

outcomes.statement: A total of 633 well-isolated units were recorded from anterior cingulate and dorsal prelimbic cortex in four rats, 411 in layer 2/3 (three rats) and 222 in layer 5 (one rat).
outcomes.source: Results, paragraph 1; Methods, Surgery and recording; Figure 2d (unit counts in the bars)
outcomes.quote: We recorded a total of 633 well-isolated units from the anterior cingulate area (area 24) and dorsal prelimbic area (area 32) of the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC)22 in four rats.
outcomes.notes: The lab's cell lists hold 627 units in three rats, EE 446, FF 146 and GG 35, within 633 +/- 63.3. No rat holds 222 +/- 22.2 under R-a (FF 146) or R-b (EE 446, GG 35). With the EE.188 behavior file's 105 cells in place of the example file's 117 the total is 615. The measured layer 5 value is FF under R-a. With every mPFC unit of the NWB files (all sorted clusters) the total is 1,373 (EE 1,155, FF 162, GG 56), outside 633 +/- 63.3, and no rat holds 222 +/- 22.2, so under that list the outcome would be not reproduced. The partial outcome rests on taking the lab's lists as the paper's units, and that check is partly circular, as the lists were adopted in part because their total is near 633. No session has 142 units in either list (largest 117 in the lab's lists, 231 among the NWB mPFC units).
deviations: Units are the lab's per-session lists (CellsInfo; for EE.188 the example file's 117 cells), an assumption: the CRCNS description documents a 1 Hz 'Cells' list but not CellsInfo, and the lists are consistent with that rule (98.9% of listed units reach 1 Hz in the trials, 28.7% of the 746 NWB mPFC units left out); they are used because their total, 627, is within 1% of the paper's 633, while every sorted cluster of the NWB files gives 1,373. Every NWB mPFC unit is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: Rats performed the odor-place matching task at 92% correct, 91.9% in the recording sessions.
outcomes.source: Results, Medial prefrontal cortical units predict behavioral choice, paragraph 1; Methods, Behavioral task
outcomes.quote: All rats performed the task at high proficiency (mean performance, 92% correct) at the time of neurophysiological data collection ... In the recording sessions, the mean correct performance was 91.9%.
outcomes.notes: SessionNP, the trial numbers of the whl file and the NWB trials tables list the same trials in every session, and the CRCNS description says only correct trials are listed. Error trials are in neither dataset, so the criterion blocks the claim.

outcomes.statement: Individual neurons fire transiently at specific locations, but the population as a whole fires relatively uniformly over the whole maze.
outcomes.source: Results, Medial prefrontal cortical units predict behavioral choice, paragraph 3; Figure 2a and 2b
outcomes.quote: viewed as a population, the firing properties of mPFC neurons were quite homogeneous ... individual neurons fired transiently, but, as a whole, the population of neurons fired relatively uniformly over the entire apparatus
outcomes.notes: The peak positions are taken from both rate readings of the claims file (P-a occupancy normalised, P-b the Methods' PSTH). In EE.188 the peaks per tenth are 24, 0, 1, 2, 14, 5, 3, 8, 1 and 59 of 117 under P-b and 46, 1, 5, 8, 13, 2, 9, 18, 12 and 3 under P-a (11.7 expected; chi-square p < 0.001 under both), so the peak criterion fails under both; every session fails it under both. The population rate per tenth stays within 50% of its mean in EE.188 (1.84 to 2.85 Hz, mean 2.30) and in 11 of 13 sessions. The layer 5 session of Figure 2a is not in the datasets; FF.130 is shown as a stand-in and fails the peak criterion too.
deviations: The thresholds (twice or half the share; 50% of the mean) are the claims file's standard choices.
The layer 5 Figure 2a session (142 cells) is not in the datasets.

outcomes.statement: About 10% of layer 2/3 neurons and 20% of layer 5 neurons fire at least one spike in a given 100 ms window, a fraction relatively constant over the maze.
outcomes.source: Results, Medial prefrontal cortical units predict behavioral choice, paragraph 3; Figure 2c; Discussion, Behavior-dependence of short-term plasticity in mPFC, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: the population firing rates (Fig. 2b) and the fraction of simultaneously active neurons (10% and 20% in 100-ms windows, layers 2/3 and 5, respectively; Fig. 2c) were relatively constant in all segments of the maze
outcomes.notes: Under R-a, reading (b), layer 2/3 sessions have 12.6% of neurons active per 100 ms window (outside 10 +/- 1) and layer 5 sessions 20.3% (within 20 +/- 2); both are constant within 50% over the tenths of the maze. Under reading (a) EE.188 has 11.8% and the FF.130 stand-in 21.9%. Under R-b neither layer matches (14.9% and 14.0%; 15.9% and 9.3%). The criterion defines only the reproduced outcome; one of its two values and the constancy hold, so the outcome is partial. With every NWB mPFC unit as the session's neurons the values fall (R-a layer 2/3 6.7%, layer 5 18.6%; EE.188 6.5%), again with one of the two values within tolerance under any reading. The round-1 verifier gives not reproduced, as no reading has both values within tolerance; the partial outcome is kept and the disagreement recorded under verifications.
deviations: The layer 5 Figure 2a session is not in the datasets; FF.130 stands in for reading (a).

Units are the lab's per-session lists (CellsInfo; for EE.188 the example file's 117 cells), an assumption: the CRCNS description documents a 1 Hz 'Cells' list but not CellsInfo, and the lists are consistent with that rule (98.9% of listed units reach 1 Hz in the trials, 28.7% of the 746 NWB mPFC units left out); they are used because their total, 627, is within 1% of the paper's 633, while every sorted cluster of the NWB files gives 1,373. Every NWB mPFC unit is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: Most neurons are active over a similar stretch of the maze, 0.27 (62 cm) +/- 0.17 (39 cm) of normalised length (mean +/- s.d.), measured between the 50% boundaries of the peak rate.
outcomes.source: Results, Medial prefrontal cortical units predict behavioral choice, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 2B
outcomes.quote: most neurons were generically active for similar standardized distances of 0.27 (62 cm) ± 0.17 (39 cm) (mean ± s.d.) in the maze (as determined by the 50% firing boundaries of the peak firing rate
outcomes.notes: Five of 24 combinations put both values within tolerance, P-a (b)(i)(x) 0.241 +/- 0.169, P-a (c)(i)(x) 0.240 +/- 0.177, P-b (a)(ii)(x) 0.234 +/- 0.154, P-b (a)(ii)(y) 0.286 +/- 0.185 and P-b (b)(ii)(y) 0.267 +/- 0.169. Other combinations give means from 0.161 to 0.416. The measured values are P-a (b)(i)(x), the first listed reading that matches (occupancy normalised rate, left and right trials as separate curves, contiguous run, the Figure 2a session).

outcomes.statement: Population vector correlations fall off over similar distances throughout the maze, 0.18 +/- 0.087 of normalised length in layer 2/3 and 0.27 +/- 0.13 in layer 5.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure 2A
outcomes.quote: Neuronal populations were relatively evenly correlated throughout the maze segments with 0.18(41cm) ± 0.087(29cm) (L2/3) and 0.27(62cm) ± 0.13(30cm) (L5) in normalized length
outcomes.notes: With raw rates the correlation between positions stays above half its diagonal value over the whole maze (width about 1.0 in every reading), as rate differences between neurons dominate it, so a normalisation of each neuron's rate is needed that the paper does not state. With each neuron's rate normalised to its peak (the assumption, as Figure 2a displays the rates), layer 5 is within tolerance (FF.130 stand-in 0.358 to 0.398, all FF sessions 0.324 to 0.359, within 0.27 +/- 0.13) and layer 2/3 just outside (EE.188 0.268 to 0.314, against the limit 0.267). With rates z-scored per neuron both layers are within tolerance (EE.188 0.185 to 0.219, all FF 0.208 to 0.238), with s.d. 0.022 to 0.052, below the paper's 0.087 and 0.13. Under the adopted normalisation layer 5 matches and layer 2/3 does not under any reading. The measured value (P-b, reading (a)) is 0.282, 0.015 above the limit, and the closest (reading (b)) 0.268, 0.001 above it. One value matches, so the outcome is partial (changed from not reproduced after verification round 1). The measured values are P-b, reading (a), peak normalised, EE.188 and FF.130. The question is for the paper's authors (findings).
deviations: The paper does not say how the rates enter the population vectors; with raw rates the measure is degenerate. Each neuron's rate is normalised to its peak, the normalisation Figure 2a states; the z-scored reading, which reproduces, is shown.
The layer 5 session is not identified; FF.130 and all FF sessions stand in.

outcomes.statement: Layer 5 neurons fire at higher mean rates than layer 2/3 neurons, over all neurons (222 against 411) and over putative pyramidal cells (85 against 133), both at P < 0.01 by t-test; putative interneurons (47 against 37) carry no significance mark.
outcomes.source: Figure 2d
outcomes.quote: Mean firing rates of the neuronal populations (± s.d.)

statistics.about: putative pyramidal cells, layer 5 against layer 2/3

outcomes.notes: Under R-a, rates over trials, layer 5 pyramidal cells fire at 3.02 +/- 3.12 Hz against 1.74 +/- 2.67 Hz (54 against 211 cells; Student p = 0.0028, Welch p = 0.0077), but all neurons differ at p = 0.045 (Student) and 0.026 (Welch), not below 0.01 (3.05 against 2.28 Hz). Over the whole session neither reaches 0.01. Interneurons 5.29 against 5.30 Hz (p = 1.0). Under R-b, EE as layer 5 gives layer 5 lower, GG as layer 5 gives 4 pyramidal cells. Bars read from Figure 2d were near 3.6 and 2.0 Hz (all) and 2.9 and 1.6 Hz (pyramidal). With every NWB mPFC unit, all neurons differ strongly under R-a (2.77 against 0.99 Hz, Student p = 7.6e-13), but that list has no cell types for the units the lab left out, so the pyramidal comparison cannot be made on it; one of the two parts holds under either list.
deviations: Cell types from the jitter test of this attempt (B-a, W-a, C-a), which finds far fewer interneurons than the paper (23 against 84).

Units are the lab's per-session lists (CellsInfo; for EE.188 the example file's 117 cells), an assumption: the CRCNS description documents a 1 Hz 'Cells' list but not CellsInfo, and the lists are consistent with that rule (98.9% of listed units reach 1 Hz in the trials, 28.7% of the 746 NWB mPFC units left out); they are used because their total, 627, is within 1% of the paper's 633, while every sorted cluster of the NWB files gives 1,373. Every NWB mPFC unit is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: Single layer 5 neurons discriminate left from right trials over a larger fraction of the maze than layer 2/3 neurons, for all neurons (P < 0.05), putative pyramidal cells (P < 0.01) and putative interneurons (P < 0.01), by t-test.
outcomes.source: Figure 2e
outcomes.quote: Mean fraction of maze lengths discriminated by firing rates of single neurons (± s.d.)

statistics.about: putative pyramidal cells, layer 5 against layer 2/3

outcomes.notes: Under R-a, reading (a), all neurons 0.263 against 0.222 (Student p = 0.077), pyramidal cells 0.331 against 0.244 (p = 0.023), interneurons 0.123 against 0.235 (4 against 19 cells, layer 5 lower); reading (b) gives the same pattern (pyramidal p = 0.015). Only one group is higher at p < 0.05, and none at the paper's levels. Under R-b no group is higher at p < 0.05.
deviations: Cell types from the jitter test of this attempt (B-a, W-a, C-a).

outcomes.statement: Left and right running paths overlap in the central arm and diverge significantly from position 0.30; head directions diverge from 0.24.
outcomes.source: Results, Medial prefrontal cortical units predict behavioral choice, paragraph 4; Supplementary Figure 3B
outcomes.quote: Left and right lap trajectories in segments 0 to 0.3 of the central arm overlapped; they began to differ significantly at position 0.3 ... Significant separation of left/right trajectories and head directions emerged at position 0.30 and 0.24, respectively (p<0.01)

statistics.test: permutation test with global bands, left and right labels shuffled

outcomes.notes: In EE.188 the lateral head position first differs globally at 0.30, within 0.30 +/- 0.03; head direction differs from 0.02, outside 0.24 +/- 0.024. Over sessions the path's first significant position ranges from 0.02 to 0.43 (0.27 to 0.30 in six of 13). Head direction exists only in the three sessions with two tracked LEDs (EE.152 0.04, EE.165 0.26, EE.188 0.02). With 1,000 permutations the global band at level 0.01 cannot be broken in EE.188 (band index 0), so 10,000 are used. Checks of the head direction: the LED 1 to LED 2 axis points along the direction of movement in the central arm (circular mean -5, -8 and -5 deg, resultant length 0.99, 0.94 and 0.98 in EE.152, EE.165 and EE.188). In EE.188 the mean head angle relative to the central arm is -95 and -82 deg on left trials and -121 and -121 deg on right trials at positions 0 and 0.02 (the turn out of the start box), meets near 0.1 (-10 and -11 deg) and separates again (-3 and 5 deg at 0.3). Angles taken relative to the circular mean of all trials at each position, which cannot wrap, give the first significant position 0.03; under both angle readings a second significant run starts at 0.23, within 0.24 +/- 0.024, but the criterion takes the first. The early difference is therefore real and not an artefact of wrapping.
deviations: The lateral axis is the perpendicular to the session's mean central-arm direction (position 0 to 0.3), in camera pixels (the image scale is not documented, which does not move where a difference begins).
M = 10,000 permutations, a choice; the paper gives no M, and with 1,000 the stepping procedure at level 0.01 settles on the outermost band.

outcomes.statement: In the side arms (positions 0.5 to 1) the fraction of neurons firing differently on left and right trials is almost twice as large in layer 5 (40%) as in layer 2/3 (22%).
outcomes.source: Results, Medial prefrontal cortical units predict behavioral choice, paragraph 4; Figure 2b
outcomes.quote: The fraction of trajectory-selective neurons in the side arms (positions 0.5-1) was almost twice as large in deep (layer 5, 40%) than in superficial (layer 2/3, 22%) neurons
outcomes.notes: Under R-a, reading (a), layer 5 61.0% (89/146) and layer 2/3 52.6% (253/481), one-sided Fisher p = 0.046; reading (b) 60.3% and 49.9%, p = 0.017. Neither value is within tolerance (40 +/- 4, 22 +/- 2.2). Under R-b, EE as layer 5 gives 53.6% against 56.9% and GG as layer 5 gives 40.0% against 55.4%, with layer 5 not above layer 2/3. One random relabelling of each neuron's trials gives 3.3%, so the test holds its level; per session the fraction ranges from 31% to 73%. With every NWB mPFC unit, R-a, reading (a), layer 5 58.6% (95/162) and layer 2/3 33.8% (409/1,211), Fisher p = 1.2e-09, neither within tolerance, so the outcome is the same under both unit lists. These variant counts move by one unit between runs of the same seeded code (the round-2 verifier's executed copy had 408/1,211, 33.7%, p = 1.1e-09).
deviations: The datasets give the lab's positions (0 at the end of the last poke, 1 at the start of reward consumption) and correct trials only, so of readings N, E and T only N-a, E-b and T-a can be run.

Units are the lab's per-session lists (CellsInfo; for EE.188 the example file's 117 cells), an assumption: the CRCNS description documents a 1 Hz 'Cells' list but not CellsInfo, and the lists are consistent with that rule (98.9% of listed units reach 1 Hz in the trials, 28.7% of the 746 NWB mPFC units left out); they are used because their total, 627, is within 1% of the paper's 633, while every sorted cluster of the NWB files gives 1,373. Every NWB mPFC unit is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: A smaller fraction of neurons, 16% in layer 2/3 and 18% in layer 5, fire differently on left and right trials already in the central arm (positions 0 to 0.3), where paths and head directions are apparently indistinguishable.
outcomes.source: Results, Medial prefrontal cortical units predict behavioral choice, paragraph 4; Figure 2b
outcomes.quote: a sizable but smaller fraction of neurons in both layer 2/3 and layer 5 (16% and 18%, respectively; Fig. 2b) was also differentially active in the central arm (segments 0-0.3)
outcomes.notes: Pooled 30.1% (189/627) of neurons have a significant segment in 0 to 0.3, against 1.4% (9/627) after one random relabelling (one-sided Fisher p = 6e-52). By layer under R-a 30.4% (layer 2/3) and 29.5% (layer 5), and under all readings 22.9% to 30.7%, none within 16 +/- 1.6 or 18 +/- 1.8. With every NWB mPFC unit (1,373 units) the fractions fall, and under R-b2 (GG layer 5), reading (b), both are within tolerance (layer 2/3 16.2%, layer 5 17.9%); under R-a layer 2/3 is within (17.2%, and 15.2% in this run, 15.3% in the round-2 verifier's copy) and layer 5 not (26.5%, 24.1%). The outcome therefore rests on the unit list, the lab's lists being adopted as the paper's units.
deviations: Units are the lab's per-session lists (CellsInfo; for EE.188 the example file's 117 cells), an assumption: the CRCNS description documents a 1 Hz 'Cells' list but not CellsInfo, and the lists are consistent with that rule (98.9% of listed units reach 1 Hz in the trials, 28.7% of the 746 NWB mPFC units left out); they are used because their total, 627, is within 1% of the paper's 633, while every sorted cluster of the NWB files gives 1,373. Every NWB mPFC unit is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: About a quarter of neurons (26% in one layer 2/3 session) fire at significantly different rates during nose poking for the two odors.
outcomes.source: Results, Medial prefrontal cortical units predict behavioral choice, paragraph 4; Supplementary Figure 6B
outcomes.quote: Approximately one-quarter of the neurons showed significantly different ... firing rates in response to one of the two odorants ... Although 26% of neurons showed significant odor preference (t-test, p<.05)
outcomes.notes: Reading (q), EE.188, Student 45.3% (53/117), Welch 42.7%; all neurons 32.4% and 32.9%. Reading (p), the sensor-timed pokes (EE and FF sessions), EE.188 about 44% and 40%, all neurons about 32% and 31% (exact values in the output). None is within 26 +/- 2.6. In EE.188 left (chocolate in the paper's example rat) pokes last 4.97 s and right pokes 3.71 s (median), as Supplementary Figure 6A notes for its rat.
deviations: Reading (p) uses the sensor envelope above 20% of its median within the poke window, a standard choice; it is not available for GG (no sensor channel) or EE.088 (no wideband signal).

outcomes.statement: Neurons' odor preference during nose poking is unrelated to their left-right differences in the stem and side arms, so odor traces do not explain the stem selectivity.
outcomes.source: Results, Medial prefrontal cortical units predict behavioral choice, paragraph 4; Supplementary Figure 6B
outcomes.quote: we ruled out this possibility after examining, and finding no reliable relationship among, the differential firing patterns in the stem area and during nose poking
outcomes.notes: In EE.188 with odor selectivity from reading (q), Student, the Fisher tests find no association with stem selectivity (odds ratio 1.17, p = 0.705) or side-arm selectivity (1.32, p = 0.576), but the correlation reading finds one, between the nose-poke rate difference and the mean left-right difference in the stem (r = -0.38, p = 2.1e-05) and in the side arms (r = -0.20, p = 0.032). Welch and reading (p) give the same pattern (stem r = -0.38 and -0.36). Over all sessions the Fisher test of the stem is also significant (odds ratio 1.76, p = 0.002).

outcomes.statement: Only a small fraction of neurons fire differently according to the reward location of the previous trial.
outcomes.source: Results, Medial prefrontal cortical units predict behavioral choice, paragraph 4; Supplementary Figures 7 and 8
outcomes.quote: found only spare evidence that any neurons fired differentially on the basis of previously visited positions ... Note that only a small fraction of neurons show retrospective coding
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), EE.188, previous-trial labels 4.3% (5/117) against current labels 60.7%. Reading (b), under every rat reading, each layer's previous-trial fraction is 5.7% to 8.9% against current 51.4% to 66.4%, below half. The null relabelling gives 4.8%, near the previous-trial fractions.
deviations: The previous trial is the previous listed (correct) trial, since error trials are not in the datasets.

outcomes.statement: Firing rates show no net positive relationship with running speed; the distribution of rate-speed correlations is symmetric around zero.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure 3C
outcomes.quote: The symmetry of these histograms around 0 suggests that, unlike in the hippocampus, this population of neurons does not exhibit a net positive relationship between firing rate and speed.
outcomes.notes: Over 627 neurons the median rate-speed correlation is -0.022 (mean -0.029, 44% positive, range -0.51 to 0.64); the two-sided Wilcoxon test finds it below 0 (p = 7.5e-05), not above. Pyramidal cells median -0.022 (p = 0.016), interneurons -0.046 (p = 0.25). The statement's symmetry around zero holds approximately, with a small negative shift.
deviations: Speed from the LED midpoint where two LEDs are tracked, from LED 1 elsewhere (ten sessions have one), in pixels per second.

outcomes.statement: Of 62,408 directed pairs of simultaneously recorded neurons, 495 (0.79%) show a short-latency narrow peak or trough in the cross-correlogram by the jitter test, 0.55% excitatory and 0.24% inhibitory, and 0.17% of pairs are reciprocally connected.
outcomes.source: Results, Characterization of mPFC neurons and their connections, paragraph 5; Figure 3a and 3e; Methods, Identifying monosynaptic interactions
outcomes.quote: Of the 62,408 cell pairs (counting each literal pair twice, corresponding to the two directions), 495 (0.79%) had short latency ... 0.55% excitatory connections and 0.24% inhibitory connections (single directions); 0.17% of cell pairs were connected reciprocally
outcomes.notes: Over 40,240 directed pairs, (B-a, W-a) 1.449% connected, 1.173% excitatory, 0.278% inhibitory, reciprocal 0.199% of directed pairs; (B-a, W-b) 1.382, 1.103, 0.278, 0.162; (B-b, W-a) 1.091, 0.917, 0.179, 0.102; (B-b, W-b) 1.071, 0.897, 0.179, 0.089 (0.179% of unordered pairs). None of the three directed percentages is within tolerance under any combination; the excitatory rate is 1.6 to 2.1 times the paper's. Per session 0% (GG.149) to 2.75%. Of the 43 connections the lab lists for EE.188, 35 to 40 are found. Jittering the spikes of one neuron only (Supplementary Figure 9A, B-a W-a) finds more connections, 1.521% connected, 1.285% excitatory and 0.236% inhibitory, so the variant does not explain the excess.
deviations: Three rats of four; the pair count is reported, not judged.

outcomes.statement: By their cross-correlogram interactions 32.5% of units are putative pyramidal cells and 12.5% putative interneurons; 50.7% of the targets of excitatory cells themselves suppress other neurons; the ratio of putative pyramidal cells to interneurons is 2.82 +/- 0.51 (s.d.).
outcomes.source: Results, Characterization of mPFC neurons and their connections, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: a sizable fraction of the recorded units could be classified as putative pyramidal cells (32.5%) or inhibitory interneurons (12.5%). A large percentage of the postsynaptic targets of the putative excitatory cells (50.7%) were suppressing other neurons ... The ratio of putative principal cells to inhibitory interneurons in the entire population, identified by physiological criteria, was 2.82 ± 0.51 (s.d.)
outcomes.notes: (B-a, W-a, C-a) 42.3% pyramidal, 3.7% interneurons (23 units), 25.5% of 184 excitatory targets with a trough, ratio 14.75 +/- 10.06 per session (11.52 pooled). Over all combinations pyramidal 37.5% to 45.1%, interneurons 2.6% to 4.4%, targets with a trough 9.4% to 25.5%, ratio 9.9 to 14.8; none within tolerance. 26 to 39 units have both a peak and a trough. Of the 476 units the lab's CellsInfo codes pyramidal, 227 are pyramidal here; of the 82 it codes interneurons, 15 are interneurons here. Of the 112 inhibitory connections (B-a, W-a), 58 lie in a pair with an excitatory peak in the reverse direction and 57 of the 80 reciprocal pairs are such an excitatory and inhibitory pair; in the CCGs printed the surrogate mean is raised by the jittered peak (EE.152 84 -> 78, 34.0 to 38.6 in the 1 to 4 ms bins against real 16 to 24, beside a peak of 194), so many troughs may come from the peak; leaving them out would lower the interneuron count further.
deviations: Cell types follow from this attempt's connections; the paper's classification is not deposited except as the lab's CellsInfo codes, which disagree between the two EE.188 files (findings).

outcomes.statement: Monosynaptic excitation between putative pyramidal cells is rare, found in 0.12% of layer 2/3 and 0.27% of layer 5 pairs.
outcomes.source: Results, Characterization of mPFC neurons and their connections, paragraph 5; Supplementary Note, Potential caveat with the cross-correlation method, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: Monosynaptic excitation between putative pyramidal cells was detected in 0.12% of layer 2/3 and 0.27% of layer 5 pairs
outcomes.notes: Under R-a, (B-a, W-a), 86 pyramidal to pyramidal connections in layer 2/3 (0.261% of 32,926 directed pairs; 1.146% of pyramidal pairs) and 26 in layer 5 (0.355% of 7,314; 1.906%), layer 5 above layer 2/3 under both denominators; (B-b, W-b) 0.228% and 0.369%. No value within tolerance. Under R-b, EE as layer 5 reverses the order.

outcomes.statement: The connection probability between nearby (under 200 um) putative pyramidal cells and interneurons is 1 to 2%.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Note, Potential caveat with the cross-correlation method, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: The 1-2% connection probability we detected between the physiologically identified nearby (<200 μm) pyramidal cell-interneuron pairs by the cross-correlation method
outcomes.notes: Same-shank pyramidal to interneuron pairs are connected in 58 of 128 (45.3%, B-a W-a) to 56 of 95 (58.9%, B-b W-b) under both direction readings, far above 0.9 to 2.2%. The interneurons are few (16 to 26) and are defined by their own troughs, which selects connected cells. The count of excitatory connections now uses the set of excitatory connections; the values are unchanged.

outcomes.statement: In the single layer 2/3 session of Figure 3b (117 neurons, 117 squared pairs) 48 connections have a putative pyramidal reference cell and 30 a putative interneuron; in the layer 5 session of Supplementary Figure 11 (142 neurons) the numbers are 73 and 25.
outcomes.source: Figure 3b legend; Results, Characterization of mPFC neurons and their connections, paragraph 6; Supplementary Figure 11 legend
outcomes.quote: Figure 3b illustrates significant peaks and troughs of crosscorrelograms of 1172 pairs of layer 2/3 cells (13,572 matrix points) simultaneously recorded in a single session
outcomes.notes: EE.188 has 117 cells and 13,572 ordered pairs, as the paper. Directed connections with a pyramidal reference cell 119 (B-a W-a) to 81 (B-b W-b), with an interneuron reference 22 to 16; distinct reference cells 67 to 59 and 16 to 9; none within 48 +/- 4.8 and 30 +/- 3. No session has 142 cells (largest FF session 64), so the layer 5 values cannot be tested. Of the lab's 43 listed connections (pairs_all), 40 are found (B-a W-a), all as excitatory. The NWB files hold no session of 142 mPFC units either. With the one-cell jitter, 137 and 15 directed connections, and 40 of the 43 listed.
deviations: The layer 5 session of Supplementary Figure 11 is not in the datasets.

outcomes.statement: A large part of the recorded neurons belong to a single interconnected circuit, 39 of 117 (33%) in the layer 2/3 session and 45 of 142 in the layer 5 session.
outcomes.source: Figure 3d; Results, Characterization of mPFC neurons and their connections, paragraph 7; Supplementary Figure 11C
outcomes.quote: a large portion of the active neurons (39 of the 117) belonged to a single interconnected circuit ... a large fraction (45 of 142 total) belonged to a single "hub" of network
outcomes.notes: The largest connected circuit of EE.188 holds 86 (B-a W-a), 85, 65 and 65 of 117 cells (93 with the one-cell jitter), outside 39 +/- 3.9. The lab's own connection list in EE188_example.mat gives a largest circuit of exactly 39 cells, so the file holds the paper's Figure 3d network and the difference comes from the connections detected here. The layer 5 session is not in the datasets (FF.130 stand-in 44 of 64).

outcomes.statement: Most connected pairs are on the same shank and connection probability falls rapidly with the distance between the neurons, yet connections are found up to 1,200 um apart.
outcomes.source: Figure 3f; Results, Characterization of mPFC neurons and their connections, paragraph 7
outcomes.quote: most functionally connected pairs were detected locally and recorded by the same probe shank. The probability of putative connections decreased rapidly as a function of distance between the somata of the recorded pair (Fig. 3f), but connections were detected between neurons up to 1,200
outcomes.notes: (B-a, W-a) 384 connected pairs on the same shank against 200 on other shanks; same-shank probability 6.77% [5.93, 7.67] against 1.29% [1.01, 1.62] at 200 um, intervals separate; excitatory probability falls from 5.95% to 0.85% to 0.31% at 0, 200 and 400 um. A connection exists at 1,400 um (one excitatory pair of 504), so the largest separation is not 1,200 um. (B-b, W-b) gives the same pattern (278 against 155; 1,400 um).
deviations: Distance is shank separation at 200 um per shank, as the criterion says.

outcomes.statement: Large fractions of putative pyramidal cells (72.2% in layer 2/3, 84.7% in layer 5) and of putative interneurons (58.3% and 83%) are trajectory specific.
outcomes.source: Results, Characterization of mPFC neurons and their connections, paragraph 7; Figure 3c; Supplementary Figure 11B
outcomes.quote: In addition to a large fraction of putative pyramidal cells (72.2% and 84.7% in layers 2/3 and 5, respectively), many interneurons (58.3% and 83% in layers 2/3 and 5, respectively) ... were also trajectory specific
outcomes.notes: Under R-a, reading (b), layer 2/3 pyramidal 66.8% (141/211) and interneurons 52.6% (10/19) are within tolerance; layer 5 pyramidal 72.2% (39/54) and interneurons 50.0% (2/4) are not. In EE.188 67.2% (39/58) and 42.9% (3/7). Two of four values match. Over all neurons 63.6% have a significant segment, 4.8% after a random relabelling.
deviations: Cell types from the jitter test of this attempt (B-a, W-a, C-a); only 23 interneurons.

outcomes.statement: Left- and right-specific neurons are not clustered on the probe but spread over the whole recorded volume, and neurons active at any part of the maze are found on all shanks.
outcomes.source: Results, Characterization of mPFC neurons and their connections, paragraph 7; Figure 3c; Discussion, Behavior-dependence of short-term plasticity in mPFC, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: left and right trajectory-specific neurons (Fig. 1c and Fig. 2) were not clustered together but occupied a large neuronal volume
outcomes.notes: Tested in the layer 2/3 session only: the layer 5 session of Supplementary Figure 11B is not in the datasets. In EE.188 shank against class gives chi-square 24.4, asymptotic p = 0.273, permutation p = 0.265, Cramer's V 0.26; shank against peak tenth, peaks from P-b, chi-square 62.7, p = 0.251 and 0.232, V 0.28, and from P-a 71.5, p = 0.217 and 0.173, V 0.30. Across the 10 sessions with 15 or more cells, two of the 20 permutation tests of shank against class and shank against P-b peak tenth fall below 0.05 (EE.210 shank against class, p = 0.022; FF.103 shank against P-b peak tenth, p = 0.013), and none of the ten P-a peak tests.
deviations: A permutation p-value (2,000 shufflings of the shank labels) is shown with the asymptotic one, as many cells of the tables are small.

outcomes.statement: Of 343 pairs with significant excitatory monosynaptic connections, 67 show identifiable position dependence of excess short-latency coincidences in the maze.
outcomes.source: Results, Behavioral modulation of monosynaptic interactions, paragraph 1; Figure 4b; Methods, Identifying position dependence of monosynaptic interactions; Supplementary Figure 12
outcomes.quote: Across all sessions, out of 343 pairs with significant excitatory monosynaptic connections in all sessions, 67 pairs showed identifiable position dependence in monosynaptic interactions by this measure
outcomes.notes: Of 472 excitatory connections (B-a, W-a), trials (a) 30 (6.4%) show position-dependent excess coincidences under both (i) and (ii); trials (b) 34 (7.2%) and 33 (7.0%). All are below 19.5 +/- 1.95% and above the null rates (2% for (a), binomial p = 4.9e-08; 1% for (b), p = 1.2e-18). Most come from EE.188 (8 of 119) and EE.196 (12 of 84).
deviations: M = 5,000 jitter surrogates (an assumption; the section gives no number); with 1,000 the global band at level 0.01 cannot be broken in 17 of 23 connections checked, as the discrete stepping procedure settles on the outermost band.
Coincident events are placed at the presynaptic spike, a standard choice.

outcomes.statement: In the layer 2/3 session of Figure 3d, 15 of 36 excitatory connections are active selectively in maze segments of left or right trajectories.
outcomes.source: Figure 5a legend
outcomes.quote: Putative monosynaptic connections that were active selectively in maze segments during left or right turn trajectories (15 of 36 excitatory connections; same set of neurons, and session, as in Fig. 3d)
outcomes.notes: In EE.188, 9 (trials a) or 8 (trials b) of the 119 excitatory connections found here are position dependent (7.6%); of the lab's 43 listed connections 7 or 6 (16.3%, 14.0%), of its 40 with a lab-pyramidal reference 7 or 6 (17.5%, 15.0%); against 15 of 36 (41.7%). The paper does not say how its 36 relate to the 48 of Figure 3b; the lab's list (43, 40 with a pyramidal reference) is the closest set.
deviations: As fig4-position-dependence (M = 5,000).

outcomes.statement: Pair 156-136, on different shanks, keeps steady firing rates between positions 0.2 and 0.5 on left trials, yet excess short-latency coincidences occur only between 0.4 and 0.6.
outcomes.source: Figure 4; Results, Behavioral modulation of monosynaptic interactions, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: cell pair 156-136, recorded from different electrode shanks, maintained steady firing rates between maze segments 0.2 and 0.5, yet short-latency coincident spikes significantly in excess of firing rate-controlled coincidences (the 'expected coincidence rate') occurred only between maze locations 0.4 and 0.6

statistics.test: jitter test with global bands, one-sided

outcomes.notes: Cells 156 and 136 of EE.188 are on shanks 5 and 4 (different, as Figure 4a) and connected (excitatory here and in the lab's list). On left trials the only significant region runs from 0.34 to 0.64 (58 coincident events); the end is within 0.6 +/- 0.06, the start outside 0.4 +/- 0.04. Cell 156's left-trial rate between 0.2 and 0.5 varies by 49% of its maximum, cell 136's by 61%, so 136 is not steady by the criterion. With jitter of the presynaptic cell only the region is 0.35 to 0.64. The lab's example file labels 136 as unknown, not as an interneuron.
deviations: As fig4-position-dependence (M = 5,000). Cell numbers are the CRCNS numbers, which the example file shares with the paper's figures (pair 156-136 on shanks 5 and 4, as Figure 4a).

outcomes.statement: In pair 197-201 transmission is significant only between 0.4 and 0.5 of left trials although the expected coincidence rate is as high from 0 to 0.5; pair 49-52 transmits only on left trials; pair 186-201 transmits only toward the end of the right arm although expected coincidences are higher earlier.
outcomes.source: Figure 5b; Results, Behavioral modulation of monosynaptic interactions, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: in pair 197-201, the expected coincidence rate was equally high between maze locations 0 and 0.5 of the left trials, yet significant spike transmission was detected only between maze locations 0.4 and 0.5 (Fig. 5b). In pair 49-52, the expected coincidence rate in the first two segments was equally high on left and on right trajectory trials, yet significant spike transmission was detected only on left trajectory trials. In pair 186-201, significant effects were observed only toward the end of the right arm
outcomes.notes: Pair 197-201, left trials, has its only significant region from 0.36 to 0.51, within tolerance, with expected coincidences as high at 0.1 to 0.45 (2.2, 1.8, 2.4) as at 0.45. Pair 49-52 has no significant region on either side. Pair 186-201 has its only region on right trials from 0.73 to 1.0 and none on left trials, but it starts before 0.75, the criterion's reading of the end of the arm. One of three pairs holds.
deviations: As fig4-position-dependence (M = 5,000).

outcomes.statement: In several pairs, position-dependent transmission remains after spikes are thinned so that both cells fire at a flat rate over the region examined.
outcomes.source: Results, Behavioral modulation of monosynaptic interactions, paragraph 1; Methods, Controlling for power; Supplementary Figure 13
outcomes.quote: Applying this approach, we indeed found that in several cases, the conclusion of position-dependent synaptic efficacy remained unaltered after thinning
outcomes.notes: Of the 34 position-dependent connections (all trials, reading i), region reading (a), 0.2 to 0.5, gives 7 pairs that keep a globally significant region and an unbroken part of the region in most of ten thinnings, among them 156-136 and 245-246 of EE.188 (10 of 10); region reading (b) gives none. The criterion is met under reading (a).
deviations: The position test after thinning uses M = 5,000, as fig4-position-dependence; region reading (b) extends the significant span by its own length to the right, or to the left at the end of the maze.

outcomes.statement: Comparing first spikes of trains with later spikes, about equal shares of pairs show depressing (12.7%) and facilitating (10.7%) spike transmission; 32.2% of the significant pairs are on different shanks.
outcomes.source: Figure 6c; Results, Behavioral modulation of monosynaptic interactions, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: we found that approximately equal percentages of neuron pairs showed firing pattern-dependent depressing (12.7%) and facilitating (10.7%) effects (Fig. 6c)
outcomes.notes: With the shared method's jitter (both cells, 1,000 surrogates) and each significant pair assigned to the tail of its permutation distribution, depressing pairs are 4.0% to 5.9% and facilitating pairs 6.8% to 12.5% over the eight combinations, and the share of significant pairs on different shanks 19.4% to 34.1%. Facilitation is within tolerance in three combinations ((a) y i, 10.4%; (b) y i, 9.9%; (b) y ii, 11.1%) and above the 5% null level in all eight (binomial p 0.036 to 1.5e-10), depression in none (p = 0.18 or more), so no combination has both fractions above 5%. The permutation median of the first-minus-later difference is above 0 in 76% of the tests (median 0.65): the standardized height grows with the number of spikes, so the raw sign does not say which side a pair is on. The presynaptic jitter (200) and the round-1 labelling by sign give no combination with both fractions above 5% at p < 0.05 either. The criterion as written, labelling by the sign of the raw difference, with the shared jitter gives depressing 5.3% to 7.7% and facilitating 5.0% to 11.3%; depression is above 5% at p < 0.05 in (a) x ii, (b) x i and (b) x ii (p = 0.011, 0.036, 0.0039), facilitation in the four combinations with later (y), and neither in (a) x i, so no combination has both and the outcome is the same under both labellings. The tail labelling leans to facilitation: the observed difference lies above the permutation median in 43% of the 1,158 tests (binomial p = 3.8e-06 against 50%), so part of the facilitation excess under it may come from the test. The measured values are pairs (a), later (x), peak (i). The literal reading of the criterion is asked of a reader (questions).
deviations: The side of a significant pair is the tail of the permutation distribution its difference lies in (above the permutation median depressing, below facilitating), from the Figure 6c legend ('two-sided test; one side corresponds facilitation, the other to depression'); the criterion's 'first above later' is read relative to that distribution, and the sign of the raw difference is shown as a variant.

The jitter for the standardized height is the shared method's (every spike of both cells on [-5, +5] ms, 1,000 surrogates); the presynaptic jitter of Supplementary Figure 9A (200) is a variant. Pairs with fewer than 5 first or later spikes (9 of 472 excitatory under x) are not tested.

outcomes.statement: Two putative pyramidal cells converging on one layer 2/3 interneuron behave oppositely; cell 197 depresses with spike repetition while the first spikes of cell 186 are ineffective and its later spikes drive the interneuron.
outcomes.source: Figure 6b; Results, Behavioral modulation of monosynaptic interactions, paragraphs 3 and 4; Supplementary Figure 14
outcomes.quote: Figure 6b shows a putative layer 2/3 interneuron innervated by two pyramidal cells, with ... pyramidal cell 197 showing a depressing effect with spike repetition. In contrast, the first spike of spike trains of cell 186 was ineffective
outcomes.notes: By the tail of the permutation distribution (shared jitter), 186 -> 201 is on the facilitating side under all four readings and significant at P < 0.10 under three ((x, max) p = 0.016, (x, sum) 0.050, (y, sum) 0.060); 197 -> 201 is on the depressing side under (x, max) only, not significantly (p = 0.875). By the literal sign, 197 has the first spikes above the later under every reading (13.8 against 4.3, (x, max)), its difference close to the permutation median (9.54 against 9.25). Both are on their sides under some reading and only 186 is significant, the partial outcome under either labelling. With the presynaptic jitter 197 is on the facilitating side under every reading.
deviations: As fig6-facilitation-depression (side by the tail of the permutation distribution; shared jitter).

outcomes.statement: Coincident spikes of two or more presynaptic cells within 5 ms discharge their common target interneuron supralinearly, more than the sum of their separate effects, while coincidences in windows over 10 ms add only linearly; group data come from 14 satellites.
outcomes.source: Figure 7a and 7b; Results, Behavioral modulation of monosynaptic interactions, paragraph 5; Discussion, Behavior-dependence of short-term plasticity in mPFC, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Coincident discharge of two presynaptic neurons within 5 ms was more effective than the sum of the effects of nonsynchronous spikes (Fig. 7a), and coincidence of three or four spikes resulted in a supralinear effect in various independently tested cell assemblies (Fig. 7b) ... showed only a linear additive effect on the cooperative ability of presynaptic neurons to discharge a postsynaptic partner
outcomes.notes: Satellites with at least three presynaptic pyramidal cells number 14 (with two, 17). With 5 ms windows the transmission probability after 2 coincident spikes is below both linear predictions in every satellite (mean excess -0.039 and -0.036, 0 of 14 above) and after 3 spikes in all but one, under every reading of k (spikes or cells) and of the lag (after the last or the first spike). With 20 ms windows the probability is also below the prediction, so the linear part holds and the supralinear part does not.
deviations: Events group the pooled presynaptic spikes from a spike to every spike within the window after it; the paper gives no grouping rule.

findings.statement: In the three GG sessions channels 97 and 98, which the CRCNS description gives as the right and left nose-poke sensors for rats FF and GG, carry no poke signal (equal activity on left and right pokes), and no channel from 97 to 101 does; the NWB files label channels 97 to 101 'neural'. In EE and FF the sensors are on 97 and 98 as described, and the trial's side sensor is the more active in every trial.

The two CRCNS lists of EE.188's cells disagree. EE188_Behavior_PFC.mat lists 105 cells (87 pyramidal, 18 interneurons); EE188_example.mat, which the description names as the paper's Figure 2a and 3d session, lists 117 (33 pyramidal, 15 interneurons, 69 unknown), and the types agree for 42 of the 105 common cells. DANDI:000067 uses the 105 cell list, so 12 of the paper's 117 cells are 'not used in the paper' there.

The cell types of EE188_example.mat disagree with the paper for the cells it names. Cells 32 and 72 are coded interneurons, but Figure 7a names them presynaptic pyramidal cells of a satellite, and the file's own pairs_all lists 32 as presynaptic (32 to 30, 52 and 135); cell 136, the interneuron of Figure 4, and 52 are coded unknown.
Only correct trials are listed (SessionNP, the whl trial numbers and the NWB trials tables), so the task performance and any analysis of error trials cannot be made from either dataset.

Neither dataset gives the layer of each rat's probe (the paper has three rats in layer 2/3 and one in layer 5, named E to H in Supplementary Figure 1), and they hold three rats (EE, FF, GG) whose names are not linked to the paper's; no rat holds the paper's 222 layer 5 units and no session the 142 cells of the layer 5 session of Figure 2a and Supplementary Figure 11.

Ten of the 13 working memory sessions have a single tracked LED (the whl file's second LED is zero, and the NWB files have led_1 only), so head direction, which the paper measures from two LEDs, exists only for EE.152, EE.165 and EE.188.

The linearised position d is described as 0 when the rat is not in a working memory trial and 1 at the end of the last nose poke, but it is nonzero (positions 0.02 to 0.05 above 1) through each trial's nose poke: 94% to 100% of the frames with d > 0 outside the listed trials (18% to 67% of all frames with d > 0) fall between the first poke start and the trial start, and all carry the trial's number. The description does not say so.

The CRCNS description documents a variable 'Cells' (units whose maximum rate in the trials exceeds 1 Hz) that the Behavior_PFC files do not hold, and does not describe their CellsInfo, the per-session cell list (627 units with EE.188's example file, against 1,373 sorted mPFC units in spikeph and the NWB files). CellsInfo is consistent with the 1 Hz rule (98.9% of listed units reach 1 Hz in the trials, 28.7% of those left out), but the criterion is not stated, and neither dataset marks which units are the paper's 'well-isolated' units.

The CRCNS description says that session EE0708/EE.188 includes EE188_example.mat, the file of the paper's Figures 2A and 3D, without saying where it is. The file is not in folder EE0708 or in the data set's filelist.txt, which list EE188_Behavior.mat, EE188_Behavior_PFC.mat and EE188_Behavior_CA1.mat; it is member 62 of 75 of EE.188.tar.gz, reached 1.99 GB into the 2.41 GB gzip stream, so it can be read only by streaming or downloading the session's whole archive.

In the Behavior_PFC files of all 13 working memory sessions the spikes' trial numbers (spikeLtr, spikeRtr) and positions (spikeX) cover each trial from its first nose-poke (SessionNP column 1), while the description defines the trial start as the end of the last nose-poke (column 2). 269071 of 676892 labelled spikes (22.6% to 64.1% per session) fall between the two, placed near position 0 (median spikeX 0.023 to 0.054 per session); the nose-poke lasts up to 315.6 s (FF103).

The description gives pairs_all of EE188_example.mat as the cell pairs with monosynaptic connections inferred by CCG, but it holds 43 directed pairs over 43 of the 117 cells, 40 from cells typed pyramidal and 3 from interneurons, where the paper reports 48 and 30 connections for this session (Figure 3b); its largest connected component, 39 cells, is the circuit of Figure 3d. Which selection of the connections it holds is not said.

The trial table of EE.188 (SessionNP, 42 correct trials) leaves out 3 trials that the nose-poke sensor channels 97 and 98 of EE.188.eeg and the position file show as correct (first pokes at 822.9, 2245.1 and 2370.7 s), and 1 error trial (2687.2 s). In two of the three (822.9 and 2370.7 s) the rat reaches the arm 193.4 and 176.9 s after its last poke, where the table's trials take at most 19.5 s, so they may be left out for that reason; why any are left out is not said.

outcomes.note: Difference in method. Both claims files say the claim cannot be tested when only correct trials are listed; fujisawa-2008-02 found EE188's error trials from the nose-poke sensor channels in its session tar (45 of 46 correct, 97.8%) and tested that one session of 13, while fujisawa-2008-03 kept to the trial tables of both datasets and blocked the claim.

Change in the claims file. The fractions are close (reading a, layer 5 62.3% there and 61.0% here, layer 2/3 54.3% and 52.6%) and none is within tolerance in either attempt; the merged claims file adds a partial outcome when layer 5 is above layer 2/3 by a one-sided Fisher test at p < 0.05, which fujisawa-2008-03 finds (p = 0.046).

Change in the claims file. Both find fractions near 30% in both layers (reading a, 31.4% and 26.7% there, 30.4% and 29.5% here), none within tolerance; the merged claims file adds a partial outcome when the pooled fraction is above that of a random relabelling of the trials, which fujisawa-2008-03 finds (30.1% against 1.4%).

Change in the claims file. Neither attempt has both values within tolerance; the merged claims file adds a partial outcome when the layer 5 value is above the layer 2/3 value, which holds in fujisawa-2008-03 (0.355% against 0.261%, B-a W-a). The connections also come from different global bands, the stepping procedure (G-b) there and 1% on each side here.

A difference in how nearly the same result was graded, not in the data or the test. Both find a single left-trial region (0.325 to 0.645 there, 0.34 to 0.64 here) whose end is within tolerance and start is not, with cell 136 not steady (59% and 61% of its maximum); fujisawa-2008-02 counted this as holding in part and fujisawa-2008-03 as not reproduced.

Difference in method. fujisawa-2008-02 counted a repetition only when both cells' thinned PSTHs reached the Methods' flatness target, which most thinnings did not, and found 0 of 16 pairs under reading a (2 without that condition); fujisawa-2008-03 does not make that condition and finds 7 of 34 position-dependent connections under reading a.

Difference in method. Both assume peak-normalised rates and find layer 5 within tolerance; for EE188 fujisawa-2008-02 gets 0.239 (reading a), within 0.18 +/- 0.087, and fujisawa-2008-03 0.268 to 0.314, just above the limit, from PSTHs built differently (200 binned positions there, the Methods' PSTH on 101 grid points here). With z-scored rates both attempts find both layers within tolerance.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper's full text under paper/. The verifier read the DANDI asset list and metadata and tested bands_from_curves, perm_bands, jitter_pair, classify_ccg and the first/later spike labelling on synthetic inputs. It had no attempt record and took the claims from the claims file. Its general points not tied to one claim: the clock check is weak for EE049 and GG097 (B11); answered by printing a binomial p of the decoding against chance, which names EE.049, FF.103, GG.097 and GG.149 as sessions where the check does not establish the shared clock (their spike times are identical to the lab's, which share the clock of SessionNP within CRCNS). Its requests for output (d at trial edges, the frames with d > 0 outside trials, the whl trial numbers, the band index kstar of the left-right tests: median 1, pointwise-equivalent level 0.20%, 5th to 95th percentile 0.20% to 0.80%) are added to the data check and the shared cells.

disagreements.reason: No reading has both values in tolerance. Reading (a): EE188 11.8% (needs 10 +/- 1). Reading (b), R-a: layer 2/3 12.6%, layer 5 20.3% (cell 41).

The claim's own method (raw PSTHs) gives about 1.0. Values fall in tolerance only after the author's z-scoring, which neither the paper nor the claims specify: EE188 0.19 to 0.22. With peak normalisation (as Figure 2a displays rates), layer 2/3 just misses: 0.268 against a limit of 0.267. The layer 5 value comes only from a stand-in session or the rat readings (cell 45).

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: The full executed notebook of the first revision, with its conclusions and summary, the README, the helper module, the claims file and the attempt record, with the paper's full text under paper/. Its general points not tied to one claim: findings with no printed output behind them (the NWB cell_type and lab_cell_number columns, DANDI's use of EE.188's 105-cell list, cells 32 and 72 coded interneurons and presynaptic in pairs_all), and the finding that spike times are identical "for all 627 cells", where cell 3 shows 615. Answered in the second revision: the data check now prints, per session, the NWB cell_type values and the count of lab_cell_number -1 (every unit of 11 of 13 sessions; in EE.188 and EE.210 the units with a type are exactly the Behavior_PFC CellsInfo list, 105 and 60 cells, with the same types, and the 12 other cells of EE.188's example file are 'not used in the paper'), the example file's codes for cells 32, 72, 52 and 136 and its pairs_all rows from 32 and 72 (32 to 30, 52 and 135; none from 72, so the finding now names 32 only), and the count of identical spike trains (615 of 627; the finding is corrected). The entry was re-run with python tools/entry.py all; the other numbers are as before, apart from the unit-list variant counts noted under side-arm-selectivity-by-layer and central-arm-selectivity, which differ by one unit from the verifier's copy.

paper_notes.statement: Supplementary Figure 2A does not say how the rates enter the population vectors. With raw rates the correlation between positions is near 1 over the whole maze; with rates normalised to each neuron's peak (as Figure 2a) the layer 2/3 width is 0.27 to 0.31, with z-scored rates 0.19 to 0.22. Which normalisation was used?

The number of permutations or jitter surrogates is not given for the left-right test, the trajectory test or the position test of coincidences. At level 0.01 the stepping procedure for global bands cannot reject with 1,000 (it settles on the outermost band in 17 of 23 connections checked); this attempt used 10,000 and 5,000. What M was used?

Figure 7 does not define the coincident events or the transmission window (how pooled presynaptic spikes are grouped within a window, and after which spike a target spike counts). Under the readings run here transmission is sublinear at 5 ms. How were events and transmission defined?

The paper does not say which of the datasets' rats is the layer 5 rat or which units make its 633 (the lab's cell lists hold 627 in three rats). Which rat and sessions are layer 5, and which units were counted?

Was the 99% global band of the jitter test the minimal band holding 99% of the surrogates entirely within both its sides, as the Methods' stepping procedure defines a global band, or 1% on each side, and were the cross-correlograms binned at 1 ms or 0.5 ms? With 1% on each side this attempt finds 1.449% of directed pairs connected with 1 ms bins and 1.091% with 0.5 ms, against 0.79%. How was the set of connections drawn in Figure 3d (pairs_all of EE188_example.mat, 43 connections) chosen?

entries.name: fujisawa-2008
entries.title: Behavior-dependent short-term assembly dynamics in the medial prefrontal cortex (Fujisawa et al. 2008)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Fujisawa, Amarasingham, Harrison and Buzsaki (2008) on both of the paper's datasets, DANDI:000067 (NWB files of the sorted units, the wideband signal and the head LEDs of three rats) and CRCNS pfc-2 (the lab's per-session summaries with the correct trials, the linearised position, the cell lists and, for the paper's Figure 2a session, its list of connections). It covers unit counts, position-dependent and trajectory-selective firing, population measures, odor and speed effects, the jitter test for monosynaptic connections, cell classes, position-dependent spike transmission, facilitation and depression, and presynaptic coincidence.

entries.title: Short-term assembly dynamics in rat medial prefrontal cortex (Fujisawa et al. 2008)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Fujisawa, Amarasingham, Harrison and Buzsaki (2008) on CRCNS pfc-2, which holds the prefrontal spikes, trials and positions of 13 working memory sessions of three of the paper's four rats. It compares firing along the maze, left and right selectivity, monosynaptic connections found by spike jitter, and the position and spike-order dependence of spike transmission.
